name: MonarchDnsRecordTable
title: DnsRecordTable
wrapsNative: VStack of cards, or Grid with GridRow at a regular width; MonarchCopyField for each name and value, MonarchStatusBadge for the found state
summary: The DNS records a user must add at their DNS provider to connect a custom domain or verify a sender: type, name and value with copy buttons, what each record is for, and whether public DNS already shows it.
whenToUse: On a custom domain or email sender setup screen, to list the records to create, with names relative to the user's zone and a found or waiting state per record.
whenNotToUse: For one value to copy use MonarchCopyField. For general tabular data use MonarchDataTable. For the progress of the whole connection use MonarchDomainProgress beside it.
api: init(_ records: [MonarchDnsRecord], zone: String? = nil, layout: MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout = .automatic, labels: MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels = MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchDnsRecord: Identifiable { init(id: String? = nil, type: String, name: String, value: String, purpose: MonarchDnsRecordPurpose? = nil, ttl: String? = nil, priority: Int? = nil, isFound: Bool? = nil) }
enum MonarchDnsRecordPurpose { case routing, verification, certificate, custom(String) }
enum MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout { case automatic, cards, table }

struct MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels { init(type: String? = nil, name: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, ttl: String? = nil, priority: String? = nil, status: String? = nil, found: String? = nil, waiting: String? = nil, purpose: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecordPurpose?) -> String)? = nil, copyName: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecord, String) -> String)? = nil, copyValue: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecord, String) -> String)? = nil, fullName: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, label: (@Sendable (String?) -> String)? = nil, summary: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: records
options.description: The records, in the order the user should create them. Each has a type, a full name, a value, and optionally a purpose, TTL, priority and found state (isFound: true is Found, false is Waiting, nil when not checked).

options.name: zone
options.description: The DNS zone the user manages, such as example.com. Names inside it are shown relative to it (book, @ for the apex) with "Full name: …" under the card.

options.name: layout
options.description: cards: one card per record. table: a Grid with one row per record. automatic: cards in a compact width or at accessibility text sizes, a table otherwise.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the column and term headings, Found and Waiting, the purpose headings, the spoken names of the copy fields, the full name line, the container name and the found announcement.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied text after a name or value is copied.

states.name: not checked
states.description: A record with isFound nil has no status badge; the table has no Status column when no record was checked.

states.name: waiting
states.description: isFound false shows a neutral "Waiting" status badge.

states.name: found
states.description: isFound true shows a success "Found" status badge. When the number of found records changes, "1 of 2 records found." is announced.

states.name: cards
states.description: Each record is a card with its purpose as a heading, the status, the type, the name and value copy fields, the priority and TTL when given, and the full name when it is shown relative to the zone.

states.name: table
states.description: A header row (Type, Name, Value, and Priority, TTL and Status only when a record uses them) and one row per record with small icon-only copy fields.

states.name: empty
states.description: No records draws nothing inside the named container.

appearance: Cards and the table use the surface fill with the default border and the container radius. Headings use the default text colour, terms and the full name line the muted text colour, and type, TTL and priority the code type role. The copy fields and status badges keep their own look in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web table scrolls sideways inside itself when narrow; on iOS the automatic layout switches to cards in a compact width and at accessibility text sizes instead, and the table's copy fields shorten long values in the middle. The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent: the card heading is a header for VoiceOver. TTL is a string the app formats. The web's DnsProviderGuide (provider-by-provider steps) is not part of this component. Android uses the same name and the same record model.
accessibility: The records are one container named "DNS records for <zone>" (or "DNS records").
Each card heading has the header trait, so the rotor moves between records.
A name is read as "name of the CNAME record" with its value, and its copy button as "Copy name of the CNAME record"; a value as "value of the CNAME record book".
The visible terms Name and Value are not read again, because the copy fields carry their own spoken names.
The found state is a word in a status badge, not only a colour.
When the number of found records changes, the summary "1 of 2 records found." is announced.
In the table, each row is a container read as its type and shown name, and the column headings have the header trait.
Copy buttons keep a 44-point touch target and confirm with "Copied" and an announcement.
edgeCases: A name outside the zone, or any name without a zone, is shown in full with no full name line.
The zone and names are compared ignoring case and a trailing dot.
Long values (DKIM keys) wrap in full in the cards and are shortened in the middle in the table; the copied value is always complete.
Priority and TTL appear in a card only when the record has them, and as columns only when any record has them.
The found announcement fires on a change only, not when the view first appears.

examples.title: Cards with found state
examples.code:
MonarchDnsRecordTable(
    [
        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "CNAME", name: "book.example.com", value: "domains.example.net", purpose: .routing, isFound: false),
        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "TXT", name: "_verify.book.example.com", value: "site-verification=4f1a9c2e", purpose: .verification, isFound: true),
    ],
    zone: "example.com"
)

examples.title: A table on a wide screen
examples.code:
MonarchDnsRecordTable(
    [
        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "MX", name: "example.com", value: "mx1.example.net", priority: 10),
        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "MX", name: "example.com", value: "mx2.example.net", priority: 20),
    ],
    zone: "example.com",
    layout: .table
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws Type, Name and Value in one row; the row needs about 560 points with two copy buttons, and a phone column has 306, so Type and Name share the first row and Value takes the one below.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: a phone layout wraps fields rather than shrinking them below a readable size
